title: LIVE PRECIPITATION
source_name: Iowa Environmental Mesonet (Iowa State University) CONUS NEXRAD N0Q Base Reflectivity mosaic from NOAA NWS WSR-88D Level-III (5-minute updates)
variable: N0Q base reflectivity (dBZ): raw radar echo strength from the NOAA WSR-88D network, composited every 5 minutes. Shows rain, snow, and thunderstorms in all seasons; it does not classify type, it shows intensity.
coverage: Basin rectangle lon -93..-73.5, lat 40.5..49.5 (all Great Lakes + surrounding land). Full rectangle, no shoreline cut: precipitation falls on land and water alike.
transparency: No precipitation (no radar echo) is fully transparent (alpha 0). Only pixels with a radar echo paint, from Very Light cyan/blue through Light/Moderate green to Heavy yellow/orange, Severe red, Intense magenta/purple, Extreme white.
what: Live radar precipitation right now over the Great Lakes: rain in spring/summer/fall, snow and lake-effect snow in winter, thunderstorms and hail whenever convection fires. Colors are echo intensity (dBZ): the stronger the echo, the heavier the precipitation.
why_extreme: Extreme (white, 75+ dBZ) is reserved for the most intense echoes: damaging hail, torrential downpours, tornadic storms.
